question: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Ana Catarina Mendes (S&D) Subject:

Detained in deplorable conditions in a Moroccan prison since 2010, Sahrawi human rights defender Naâma Asfari has been held in isolation for the past few days. As a form of protest, he began an indefinite hunger strike at least six weeks ago and has already lost ten kilos. Along with 17 other activists for the Sahrawi cause, Asfari is facing a lengthy prison sentence for taking part – alongside thousands of Sahrawis – in peaceful protests. According to the defence lawyers, the convictions are based on confessions extracted under torture. The Moroccan authorities are unmoved by Asfari’s pleas to transfer prisoners to Western Sahara, where they can receive family visits – something that has been blocked since 2019. It has been at least two days since there was any news from Naâma Asfari, who has not made his usual weekly telephone call. In light of international humanitarian law and the human rights that the Moroccan State is bound to uphold, and given the EU’s international and economic ties with the Kingdom of Morocco, what urgent steps are being taken to save Naâma Asfari’s life and enforce the rights of Sahrawi prisoners?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.8.2026) The EU reiterates the importance of upholding and protecting all human rights, while defending their universality. The EU recalls in particular the UN Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners1, which is an essential component of the rule of law and protection of human dignity worldwide. Respect for democratic principles and fundamental rights is an essential element of the EUMorocco Association Agreement2, which forms the foundation of EU-Morocco relations. Questions regarding human rights, including individual cases, are addressed in the framework foreseen under the Association Agreement, including a dedicated sub-committee, and other regular exchanges with the Moroccan authorities. In addition, the EU conducts a regular dialogue with civil society and non-governmental organisations that closely monitor human rights issues. The EU Delegation to Morocco also regularly coordinates locally with Member States as well as like-minded states on human rights issues. As regards Western Sahara, the EU continues to support the United Nations-led process, in line with UN Security Council resolution 2797(2025)3, and the efforts of the UN Secretary-General and his Personal Envoy to advance a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution.
